Synthetix control, copied Optimism messaging and purchased-
stable custody
1 October 2026. All blockchain operations in this study are public reads: getters, runtime bytecode,
transaction counts, logs, receipts and headers. No mint, burn, administrative call, signing or state-
changing simulation was performed. The linked L2 is reported to have a private RPC and is not
inspected. Conclusions about its deployment or operators remain conditional.
Findings
The later Safe and rollup audit (Appendix 52) extends these reads to block 27,685,402, verifies the
Optimism BondManager's proposer-only admission and finds distinct GnosisDAO and Arbitrum control
changes. The council study (Appendix 68) adds protocolDAO, Treasury, Ambassador and Grants custody
checks and separates staker elections from multisig execution authority. Those findings do not change
this study's result for the sampled Synthetix and Optimism Safes.
The selected public PulseChain controls do not establish a Synthetix or Optimism takeover. The
two controlling Safes retain inherited owners, thresholds, modules, implementations and transaction
counters. The copied Optimism registry and state-batch counters also match inherited state. A complete
bounded census of selected control events returns no postfork events for the two Safes, Synthetix
resolver or Optimism StateCommitmentChain. This does not identify who privately possesses existing
keys.
A concrete local DAI/sUSD wrapper does exist. Its cap is unchanged; its DAI reserves have declined since
the inherited snapshot, reopening capacity. The later integration and wallet audit (Appendix 69) verifies
five successful historical e121 mints, establishing operation at their recorded amounts. That evidence
advances the local recycling route beyond the getter-only checks below; it does not establish source-L2
issuance or new governance control.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 429

The relay transaction audit (Appendix 46) also verifies two postfork withdrawals using inherited
Optimism commitments. The empty selected state-batch census below concerns new batches, not every
messenger relay or token settlement.
The wrapper can hold bought pDAI as synth collateral. That changes the financial claim: the collateral
supports eligible synth redemption, including by other holders. It is not exclusively retained treasury
cash or an interest-paying deposit account. Other acquired stables can be held directly, placed in eligible
earning positions or used in supported issuer baskets, with separate custody and liquidity accounting.
Evidence checkpoints and method
The inherited reference is Ethereum chain 1 at block 17,232,999, hash 
0xe5667f9cafb115b1dcfc36b0b569a5601f01dfa000698140a1298ef4f87e2e37, matching the preserved PulseChain
boundary of 10 May 2023. Archive getters and code reads use https://eth.drpc.org with single requests.
Primary public-control reads are PulseChain chain 369 at block 27,683,800, hash 
0xb3744382d2a06dac8856f1fefe4651dd7f5a9c508f420ad97b6683636c7806a3. Wrapper/predicate and nested-Safe reads
use a separate later checkpoint, block 27,683,934, hash 
0x29fed31878085918ed1376c5c28bd7db41f4384a0966238e01401b3c5339b496. These are explicitly different checkpoints.
Older attempted wrapper reads hit pruned state and are retained as failed reads, not zeros.
The historical Synthetix package synthetix@2.88.1, published 3 May 2023, supplies primary upstream
source and deployment identities before the inherited boundary. Its downloaded tarball matches the
registry's SHA-1 and SHA-512 integrity values. Selected files and SHA-256 records are retained. This is
an upstream source/address association and inherited/current runtime comparison, not an independent
Solidity compiler reproduction. Exact wrapper and messenger sources were also fetched from the
PulseChain explorer; the selected Issuer, factory, resolver implementation and Safe singleton explorer
responses lack verified source bodies.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 430

All 13 Synthetix signer addresses return empty runtime code at the later checkpoint. Six of the seven
Optimism signer addresses do too; the seventh is the nested Safe above. The sampled control structure
therefore has no observed replacement by a token-voting owner contract or enabled voting module. This
is a claim about selected on-chain execution authority; upstream council elections and off-chain voting
instructions are different mechanisms.
The selected controller/address values identify the required contracts. They do not prove common
human control, stolen or transferred keys, ownership of any signer by the proposed group, or current
private-L2 administration. An unchanged signer can change private custody without an on-chain
ownership event. Consequently the study neither confirms that allegation nor categorically rules out
private key control.
The control-event census spans 17,233,000–27,683,800. It makes 840 contiguous, nonoverlapping
queries, each at most 50,000 blocks, across the Synthetix Safe, Optimism owner Safe, Synthetix
resolver and StateCommitmentChain. Selected events cover Safe owner/threshold/module/singleton/
execution changes, resolver imports/ownership changes and state-batch append/deletion. It returns zero
selected events, zero query errors and zero verification gaps. This bounded census is not every
event of every Synthetix component. Earlier broad queries and attempts using unsupported address-list
filters did not complete; they are not part of this successful census.
Seventeen runtime comparisons cover SNX/sUSD proxies, Synthetix, Issuer, DebtCache, SystemSettings,
SystemStatus, WrapperFactory, EtherWrapper, ExchangeRates, T okenState, FlexibleStorage,
CollateralManager, both Safe singletons, messenger implementation and StateCommitmentChain. All
match inherited bytes. Both subsequently discovered factory-wrapper runtimes also match: 19
matching runtime comparisons in total. The protocol comparison has 68 identical results of 69 reads;
the remaining getter is the changed debt-cache amount. Its cache timestamp remains 10 May 2023 and
its stale flag is true in both compared reads. Inventory/accounting changes must not be conflated with
administrative upgrades.

No administrative transaction was constructed or simulated. The table maps ordinary governance
capabilities, not proof that the proposed operator can exercise them. The current Synthetix authorization
requires the existing Safe's approval rule; the separate Optimism registry uses its own Safe. A move to a
voting controller would need an actual authorized ownership, implementation or module change, none
established by the selected evidence.
Destination messaging is a distinct proof system
The copied messenger proxy is 0x25ace71c97b33cc4729cf772ae268934f7ab5fa1; its manager resolves
implementation 0xd9166833ff12a5f900ccfbf2c8b62a90f1ca1fd5. Its verified legacy source verifies both the
accepted state commitment and message storage proof. StateCommitmentChain is 
0xbe5dab4a2e9cd0f27300db4ab94bee3a233aeb19.
The StateCommitmentChain getter sets FRAUD_PROOF_WINDOW = 604800, confirming the copied configuration's 
seven-day rule. Its getTotalBatches, getTotalElements and last sequencer timestamp match inherited state;
the last sequencer timestamp is 10 May 2023, 22:33:35 UTC. The selected postfork append/deletion
census is empty. This confirms the configured delay and absence of selected new accepted batches
through the checkpoint, rather than a live private-L2 withdrawal taking exactly seven days end to end.
The sUSD bridge additionally checks its messenger and configured source counterpart 
0x136b1ec699c62b0606854056f02dc7bb80482d63. The historical package identifies that counterpart as Optimism's
SynthetixBridgeT oBase. Its native source burn/destination mint architecture is established in SIP-229.
Historical upstream Issuer source supplies a further authorization detail missing from the explorer
response: issueSynthsWithoutDebt restricts callers to resolver-selected trusted bridges or FeePool, issues the
selected synth and updates cached debt. The recorded destination bridge is one of the relevant resolver-
selected identities. This supports the authorized issuer route; it does not execute a transfer or certify the
private source's debt state.
Arbitrum's rollup/outbox assertion system and legacy Optimism's state/message-proof system serve a
similar messaging purpose but have distinct contracts, authenticated senders, commitments and proof
formats. Owning one system does not make its assertions pass the other system automatically. A
compatible source deployment or authorized integration could connect them. The currently sampled
public Optimism configuration does not establish that connection, and no fresh postfork accepted roots
were observed in the selected component. A private RPC change alone does not establish a change in
the public destination's accepted roots or counterpart.
The actual local wrappers
The selected WrapperFactory's contract nonce is 3 both at the inherited boundary and at the public-
control checkpoint. Its published source creates Wrapper children with ordinary contract creation. The
two candidate child addresses were derived from the factory's address/nonces, then confirmed by token,
currency-key and factory isWrapper getters. Address derivation alone was not treated as proof of
registration.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 432

Both wrappers are factory-recognized, unpaused and resolver-cached at the later checkpoint. Their caps
and fees match inherited values. DAI reserves were exactly 20 million at the inherited boundary; their
decline reopened capacity without a cap increase. The WETH wrapper's raw balance increased above its
cap; the transfer provenance was not established. Copied WETH must not be equated with externally
redeemable Ethereum ETH.
An older EtherWrapper also exists at 0xc1aae9d18bbe386b102435a8632c8063d31e747c, with sampled maximum/
capacity zero. The historical package names NativeEtherWrapper 0x7a3d898b717e50a96fd8b232e9d15f0a547a7eeb,
an adapter to the older wrapper rather than an independent stablecoin collateral route. The two child
contracts are the recognized candidates discovered from this selected factory. The study does not
inventory every custom deployment or every registered CollateralManager loan contract.
Historical Optimism also had DAI and LUSD/sUSD wrapper routes; see SCCP-264 and SIP-189. That
historical fact is separate from the uninspected private L2's current contracts. No USDC, USDT, mUSD,
FRAX or MIM child was found in the selected local factory. Its owner-controlled factory design can add
approved token/synth pairs; those inputs are not currently authorized merely because they are
stablecoins or Curve coins.
What raises or lowers capacity?
The verified wrapper source defines capacity = max(maxTokenAmount − token.balanceOf(wrapper), 0). Governance
sets maxTokenAmount; user flows change the balance. Deposits consume spare capacity. Eligible burn/
redemption releases collateral and reopens capacity. Direct transfers into the wrapper also consume
capacity and do not themselves issue a depositor receipt. Lowering the cap below existing balances
makes spare capacity zero; it does not by itself remove collateral or rewrite outstanding synth claims.
Pausing and valuation rules are separate predicates.
DAI-wrapper minting checks the sUSD currency key rather than a live market price of pDAI. The sampled 
rateIsInvalid(sUSD) returns false; system/issuance suspension getters are clear. Published ExchangeRates
source treats sUSD as the unit-of-account exception. The stale general debt cache and other stale synth
feeds therefore cannot be promoted into proof that this particular wrapper's mint is disabled.
Conversely, the successful selected getters do not certify a complete funded mint: token allowances,
transfers and all dependent calls still belong to execution. No such execution was tested.
Purchased pDAI can replenish local synth inventory
Source synth → authenticated transfer → local sUSD → buy pDAI
                                                       │
                              ┌────────────────────────┼───────────────────────┐
                              ▼                        ▼                       ▼
                       Treasury inventory       Eligible LP/yield        DAI/sUSD wrapper
                       available for support    position/receipt         collateral custody
                                                                               │
                                                                       additional local sUSD
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 433

│
                                                                          further trading
For a simple fee illustration, 100 pDAI deposited into the sampled DAI wrapper produces about 99.75
sUSD for the depositor; mint fees support the protocol's fee distribution. Burning 100 sUSD through an
eligible funded wrapper redemption yields about 99.95 pDAI. These figures come from the recorded
positive fee rates and source mechanics, not a submitted quote or transaction.
If sUSD is a spendable counter-asset and pDAI can be bought for less than roughly 0.9975 sUSD per pDAI
after trade costs, this conversion can create an arbitrage incentive to buy pDAI and deposit it. The
opposite conversion offers a ceiling near 1.0005 sUSD per pDAI when eligible redemption inventory is
available. This is a bounded relationship against sUSD, not an independently proved external US-dollar
peg. Market execution, inventory, fee changes and deposit/redemption conditions determine whether
the theoretical band is accessible.
The operator need not unwrap source synths to use this branch. Purchased local pDAI itself enters the
local wrapper; newly issued sUSD can return to the market. This is a potentially simpler local recycling
mechanism than repeatedly withdrawing source collateral. It remains limited by the sampled 14.65-
million-DAI spare capacity, rather than providing demonstrated capacity for 50 billion tokens.
The deposited pDAI supports outstanding synth claims. Once the new sUSD is sold, other eligible synth
holders may acquire and burn sUSD to withdraw available pDAI. Thus depositing all acquired pDAI does
not preserve exclusive ownership or permanent removal from circulation. Directly donating pDAI to a
wrapper does not confer a private withdrawal right. The wrapper has no ordinary deposit-interest
mechanism: its role is collateral custody and issuance/redemption, while fees flow under Synthetix's own
fee system.

pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 434

These are custody/financing route families, not recommendations or certification of present yields. The 
issuer study (Appendix 38) supplies the exact sampled collateral rules. Merely placing assets in another
contract does not preserve spendable treasury ownership; the receipt, encumbrance and withdrawal rule
must be tracked. Freely available peg-support inventory, synth collateral and earning positions need
separate balances to avoid counting the same assets twice.
Reproduction and limits
Evidence is frozen in artifacts/pulsechain-susd-authority-custody-20261001/. Explicit getter manifests start
with Research/experiments/pulsechain_susd_authority_; the successful selected control-history manifest is 
pulsechain_susd_authority_control_history_20261001.json. Getter reproduction uses Research/scripts/
probe_pulsechain_routes.py --calls; older PulseChain state requires a retaining endpoint. Event reproduction
uses Research/scripts/collect_pulsechain_events.py --manifest, with 50,000-block partitions for the sampled
public endpoint. Historical Ethereum getters use --chain-id 1 --single-requests and preencoded data.
Failed broad log requests, unavailable inherited receipts, Ethereum free-plan historical log refusals, a
failed archive endpoint and pruned wrapper-state reads are retained or recorded as collection
limitations. None is interpreted as zero activity or zero balance. The successful control census is
separately validated for complete, contiguous selected ranges. Private source RPC access, private key
ownership, a working pARB-to-Optimism integration and complete mint/bridge execution remain
unresolved.
The event collector now supports bounded ranges, explicit chain identity and preservation of unavailable
receipt records as unverified evidence. It uses the same public research User-Agent as the getter probe.
A representative test checks successful receipt inclusion and the missing-receipt case without treating
incomplete evidence as verified. ./scripts/test.sh --research passed 65 tests and 82 subtests after
these changes. Earlier research archives remain frozen; the new release has its own hashes and
validation record.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 435

public Optimism configuration does not establish that connection, and no fresh postfork accepted roots
were observed in the selected component. A private RPC change alone does not establish a change in

What raises or lowers capacity?
The verified wrapper source defines capacity = max(maxTokenAmount − token.balanceOf(wrapper), 0). Governance
sets maxTokenAmount; user flows change the balance. Deposits consume spare capacity. Eligible burn/
redemption releases collateral and reopens capacity. Direct transfers into the wrapper also consume
capacity and do not themselves issue a depositor receipt. Lowering the cap below existing balances
makes spare capacity zero; it does not by itself remove collateral or rewrite outstanding synth claims.
Pausing and valuation rules are separate predicates.
DAI-wrapper minting checks the sUSD currency key rather than a live market price of pDAI. The sampled 
rateIsInvalid(sUSD) returns false; system/issuance suspension getters are clear. Published ExchangeRates
source treats sUSD as the unit-of-account exception. The stale general debt cache and other stale synth
feeds therefore cannot be promoted into proof that this particular wrapper's mint is disabled.
Conversely, the successful selected getters do not certify a complete funded mint: token allowances,
transfers and all dependent calls still belong to execution. No such execution was tested.

For a simple fee illustration, 100 pDAI deposited into the sampled DAI wrapper produces about 99.75
sUSD for the depositor; mint fees support the protocol's fee distribution. Burning 100 sUSD through an
eligible funded wrapper redemption yields about 99.95 pDAI. These figures come from the recorded
positive fee rates and source mechanics, not a submitted quote or transaction.
If sUSD is a spendable counter-asset and pDAI can be bought for less than roughly 0.9975 sUSD per pDAI
after trade costs, this conversion can create an arbitrage incentive to buy pDAI and deposit it. The
opposite conversion offers a ceiling near 1.0005 sUSD per pDAI when eligible redemption inventory is
available. This is a bounded relationship against sUSD, not an independently proved external US-dollar
peg. Market execution, inventory, fee changes and deposit/redemption conditions determine whether
the theoretical band is accessible.
The operator need not unwrap source synths to use this branch. Purchased local pDAI itself enters the
local wrapper; newly issued sUSD can return to the market. This is a potentially simpler local recycling
mechanism than repeatedly withdrawing source collateral. It remains limited by the sampled 14.65-
million-DAI spare capacity, rather than providing demonstrated capacity for 50 billion tokens.
The deposited pDAI supports outstanding synth claims. Once the new sUSD is sold, other eligible synth
holders may acquire and burn sUSD to withdraw available pDAI. Thus depositing all acquired pDAI does
not preserve exclusive ownership or permanent removal from circulation. Directly donating pDAI to a
wrapper does not confer a private withdrawal right. The wrapper has no ordinary deposit-interest
mechanism: its role is collateral custody and issuance/redemption, while fees flow under Synthetix's own
fee system.

Evidence is frozen in artifacts/pulsechain-susd-authority-custody-20261001/. Explicit getter manifests start
with Research/experiments/pulsechain_susd_authority_; the successful selected control-history manifest is 
pulsechain_susd_authority_control_history_20261001.json. Getter reproduction uses Research/scripts/

uses Research/scripts/collect_pulsechain_events.py --manifest, with 50,000-block partitions for the sampled

Failed broad log requests, unavailable inherited receipts, Ethereum free-plan historical log refusals, a

separately validated for complete, contiguous selected ranges. Private source RPC access, private key
ownership, a working pARB-to-Optimism integration and complete mint/bridge execution remain
unresolved.
The event collector now supports bounded ranges, explicit chain identity and preservation of unavailable
